turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I couldn't reproduce this, so I haven't changed any code.

I followed the whole path that runs when a meeting ends (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts` → `LLMHelper.generateMeetingSummary` → DB save → `MeetingDetails.tsx` render). Nothing in it filters action items by whether they have a date. No step checks for "due", "deadline" or a date. Whatever the model returns is stored and shown as is. The prompts in `electron/llm/prompts.ts` actually say the opposite of the bug: "Keep every action item that has an owner, even if it has no due date" (lines 39, 74, 346 and others).

So if "Priya will send the contract" is going missing, the model is leaving it out. The code isn't throwing it away. I found two places in the end-of-meeting prompts that could cause that, but I haven't confirmed either one:

1. **Mode-specific sections** (`MeetingPersistence.ts:155-191`). If a mode is active, the recap uses that mode's sections, not the generic `actionItems` list. In Team Meet and Sales, the Action Items section is defined as "All action items that were said **I** would do after the meeting" (`DatabaseManager.ts:518, 533`). That drops Priya's task because she's someone else, whether or not it has a date. It would look like your bug if most of the tasks you've seen dropped had other people on them.
2. **The Groq summary prompt** (`prompts.ts:375`). Its only example is "Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday", and it never says owner-only items count. The generic prompt in `MeetingPersistence.ts:141-203` is also missing the "keep it even with no due date" rule that the other prompts have.

To pin it down, I need a few things from you:
- Which mode was active when this happened (Team Meet, Sales, General, or none)?
- Which provider made the summary (Groq, a custom provider, or something else)?
- A meeting where it happened. A transcript snippet with the dropped line and the recap you got is enough.

If it was Team Meet or Sales, the cause is #1. Then the question is whether those sections should list everyone's tasks or only yours, because right now they're built to list only yours. Once I know which path you hit, I can make the right fix.

I found the real cause and fixed it. The recap model only ever saw the first 10,000 characters of the meeting, which is about the first 10 to 15 minutes. Tasks like "Priya will send the contract" usually come up in the wrap-up at the end, so they were cut off before the model ever read them. It wasn't really about missing deadlines. Those tasks just tend to be said late.

**How I reproduced it:** I made a read-only copy of your Natively database and checked your saved meetings. In the May 20 "Flare AI Receptionist" meeting you said "I think I'll just email her", which has an owner and no date. The recap's Action items list is empty. That line sits at character ~27,800 of a ~34,000-character transcript. The summary call cut the transcript off at 10,000 characters (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`, line 207 before my change), so the model never saw it.

**What I changed:**
- **`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`:** the recap now gets the whole transcript, up to 200,000 characters (about 50k tokens). The summary function already sends long inputs to Gemini, so that's safe. For a meeting longer than that, it keeps the start and the end and drops the middle, since the end is where tasks get handed out.
- **Same file, recap rules:** I added an explicit rule that a task someone commits to is an action item even with no date. "Priya will send the contract" becomes "Priya: Send the contract (no date given)". Your active mode is General, which uses this prompt.
- **`electron/llm/prompts.ts`:** the same rule is now in the Groq recap prompt, which only had a dated example before.

**What I couldn't check:** there's no `node_modules` in this repo, and the sandbox blocked npm, so I couldn't typecheck or run the app. I only ran a simulation on your real Flare meeting: the old 10,000-character cut misses "email her" and the new version includes it. The code change is small, but run `npm install` and record a test meeting to confirm.

Your old recaps won't update on their own. Only new meetings get the fix. Your database has no meetings after May 27. If you've seen this more recently, it was on a different install or another copy of the app.

It's still not working because the app you're running doesn't have the fix. The code I changed is a source folder that has never been built.

What I found:

- **You're running `/Applications/Natively.app`.** It's version 2.6.0, built May 10. I searched its bundled code and it still has the old `data.context.substring(0, 10000)` cut. So every recap from that app still only sees the first ~10,000 characters of the meeting.
- **My fix only exists in the source** at `<scratch>/runs/.work/0c4c46572a/repo`. That folder has no `node_modules` and no build, so nothing you can launch runs it.
- **No new meetings have been saved since May 27.** The app's database hasn't changed since July 12. If you tested it today, the meeting either never got saved or came from somewhere other than this install. Either way I have no new failing meeting to look at.

I didn't change any more code, because I can't reproduce a failure in code that has never run.

To actually test the fix, run this from that repo in your own terminal. My sandbox blocks npm, so I can't do it:

```
cd <scratch>/runs/.work/0c4c46572a/repo
npm install
npm start
```

`npm start` launches a dev copy of the app with the fix. Record a short test meeting and say a task with no date near the end ("Priya will send the contract"). That task should show up under Action items. If you want it in the installed app too, `npm run dist` builds a new `Natively.app` to replace the one in `/Applications`.

If that dev build still leaves the task out, tell me and I'll pull that meeting from the database and see what the model got and what it returned.
